title: Chimerism and phenotypic analysis of intraepithelial and lamina propria T cells isolated from human ileal biopsies after intestinal transplantation
protocol: Collect research ileoscope samples from consented patients during clinical endoscopy.
Disrupt the epithelial integrity of ileal biopsy specimens using DTT and EDTA to detach intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs).
Incubate the biopsy specimens with DTT and EDTA to liberate IELs and IECs into the medium without altering the basement membrane.
Collect supernatant from both incubation steps.
Combine collected supernatants to enrich for IELs.
Collect research samples consisting of 1–4 ileal biopsy pieces from consented patients during clinical endoscopy.
Place the sample into DTT buffer in a labeled 125 mL ventilated flask with a sterile stir bar.
Place the flask containing the buffer and sample into a prewarmed water bath at 37°C, ensuring the water level is above the buffer level in the flask.
Filter the DTT cell suspension through a 40 μm single-cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the filtered cell suspension, pour off the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL MLR media.
Add 20 mL prewarmed EDTA buffer to the flask containing the sample pieces, ensuring they are floating in the buffer.
Filter the EDTA cell suspension through a 40 μm single-cell strainer into the 50 mL conical tube from the previous DTT step with MLR media.
Add 20 mL of prewarmed DTT buffer to a sterile 125 mL flask.
Transfer ileal biopsy piece(s) into the flask so each piece floats in the DTT buffer.
Place the flask into a prewarmed water bath beaker set on a hot plate stirrer.
Incubate biopsy pieces in DTT buffer with constant stirring at 125–150 rpm for 20 min at 37°C.
Increase the stirring rate to 150–250 rpm for tissue processing.
Allow pieces to settle at the bottom of the flask and filter the DTT cell suspension through a 40 μm strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the DTT cell suspension at 465 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant to retain the cell pellet.
Add 5–10 mL MLR media to the cell pellet in the conical tube and keep it on ice.
Add 20 mL prewarmed EDTA buffer to the flask.
Incubate biopsy pieces in EDTA buffer with constant stirring at 150–200 rpm for 30 min at 37°C.
Ensure each biopsy piece is re-submerged in the new buffer before proceeding with the next incubation.
Allow pieces to settle to the bottom of the flask and filter the EDTA cell suspension through a 40 μm strainer into the 50 mL conical tube that already has the DTT cell suspension.
Centrifuge the DTT and EDTA cell suspension at 465 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant to retain the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL MLR media.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 5 mL flow cytometry tube with a cap.
Keep the tube on ice or in a refrigerator at 4°C.
Add 25 mL of prewarmed LPL buffer to the 125 mL flask, ensuring the biopsies are submerged in the LPL buffer.
Filter the LPL cell suspension through a 40 μm single-cell strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the sides of the 125 mL flask with 25 mL MLR media.
Filter the washed contents through a 40 μm single-cell strainer into the same 50 mL conical tube containing the LPL cell suspension.
Incubate the tissue suspension at 37°C and 150–200 rpm for 1–1.5 hours.
Monitor the water bath temperature periodically during longer incubation periods.
Pour the LPL cell suspension through a 40 μm strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the sides of the 125 mL flask with 25 mL MLR media and pour it through a 40 μm strainer into the 50 mL conical tube containing the LPL cell suspension.
Centrifuge the mixture at 465 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant to retain the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL MLR media.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a new 5 mL flow cytometry tube with a cap.
Keep the tube on ice or in a refrigerator at 4°C.
Perform fluorescence compensation on the BD LSR II flow cytometer for the antibody panel used in patient sample analysis.
Stain single color controls using PBMCs isolated from a healthy human donor for each fluorophore, at a ratio of 0.5 × 10^6 cells per control.

Acquire each single-color control on the flow cytometer and adjust voltage settings to maximize mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) for the target fluorophore while minimizing spillover in other channels.
Compensate the full panel based on acquired data from single color controls.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer to each flow cytometry tube.
Centrifuge samples at 465 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant and touch the tube rim with a clean Kim Wipe while inverted to absorb any last drops of supernatant.
Resuspend cells at 10 × 10^6 cells/mL in FACS buffer.
Stain each cell sample with Fc block, pipetting up and down to mix.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Stain each sample with the prepared primary antibody master mix.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C in the dark, ideally in a fridge at 4°C.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer to each flow cytometry tube.
Centrifuge samples at 465 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant and touch the tube rim with a clean Kim Wipe to absorb any last drops of supernatant while keeping the tube inverted.
Reconstitute cells at 10 × 10^6/mL in FACS buffer by adding 50 μL FACS buffer to 0.5 × 10^6 cells per tube.
Stain each sample with the secondary antibody (Streptavidin BUV737).
Incubate for 15 min at 4°C in the dark.
Reconstitute cells at 10 × 10^6/mL in FACS buffer.
Add 50 μL of FACS buffer to 0.5 × 10^6 cells per tube.
Centrifuge samples at 465 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant.
Touch the tube rim with a clean Kim Wipe to absorb any last drops of supernatant while keeping the tube inverted.
Stain each sample with DAPI by adding 5 μL of DAPI staining solution per 1 × 10^6 cells and pipetting up and down to mix.
Keep cell samples at 4°C in the dark before proceeding to next steps.
Pause point: The experiment can be paused for up to 12 h at this point before proceeding. Samples should be kept at 4°C in the dark during this period.
Collect data on the flow cytometer (LSR II, BD Biosciences).
Perform fluorescence compensation prior to acquiring patient samples.
Adjust settings on the flow cytometer.
Perform HLA quality control using pre-transplant donor and recipient PBMCs or lymphoid tissue cells with known HLA typing.
Use commercially available HLA antibodies that work best for chimerism tracking on post-transplant specimens.
Isolate PBMCs from a healthy human donor to serve as a staining control.
Stain the control PBMCs with the same antibodies used for patient samples.
Acquire both stained control and patient samples on the flow cytometer.
Determine chimerism gating and resting stage phenotypic markers using the control sample.
Gate on the control sample first, then apply those gates to patient samples.
Adjust lineage markers and chimerism gates based on contour plot distribution.
